record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: Can one develop a rigorous theory of shock layers and boundary layers for the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation, including both the construction of matched asymptotic expansions and the convergence analysis needed to justify those asymptotics in the hydrodynamic limit?

evidence.quote: Even a formal asymptotic theory for the shock layer and boundary layer problems has not been achieved.
it is of fundamental importance to understand the fluid dynamic approximation to the nonlinear Boltzmann equation in the presence of shocks and boundaries.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Boltzmann equation
  ∂_t F + v · ∇_x F = (1/ε) Q(F,F),
for the one-particle distribution F(t,x,v) ≥ 0 with x in a domain Ω ⊂ R^d (possibly with boundary ∂Ω on which a kinetic boundary condition such as diffuse reflection or specular reflection is prescribed), v ∈ R^d, and collision operator Q corresponding to a physical interaction (e.g. hard spheres or a hard/soft potential with angular cutoff). Here ε > 0 is the Knudsen number.

In the hydrodynamic (small-Knudsen) limit ε → 0, the macroscopic fields (density, momentum, temperature) of F are formally governed by the compressible Euler equations, whose solutions may develop shock discontinuities and which must be supplemented by boundary conditions at ∂Ω. Near shock hypersurfaces and near ∂Ω one expects thin transition regions — shock layers (of width O(ε)) and Knudsen boundary layers (of width O(ε)) — across which F is not close to a local Maxwellian.

Develop a rigorous mathematical theory of these layers for the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation. Specifically:

(a) Construct matched asymptotic expansions of solutions F^ε in the limit ε → 0, consisting of an interior (Hilbert/Chapman–Enskog) expansion away from shocks and boundaries, together with shock-layer expansions (of travelling-wave type) attached to each Euler shock and boundary-layer expansions (of Knudsen-layer type) attached to ∂Ω, with appropriate matching conditions tying together the inner and outer expansions.

(b) Prove convergence of true solutions F^ε of the nonlinear Boltzmann equation to the composite asymptotic expansion as ε → 0, with quantitative error estimates in suitable norms, thereby justifying the fluid-dynamic approximation by the compressible Euler equations in the presence of both shocks and physical boundaries.

Is such a rigorous theory — formal construction together with convergence proof — achievable for the genuine (non-model) nonlinear Boltzmann equation?
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial progress has been made. For the Broadwell and other discrete-velocity models, boundary-layer and shock-layer fluid-dynamic limits are established (Caflisch–Nicolaenko, Xin and collaborators). For the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation with hard-sphere or soft-potential collisions, hydrodynamic limits to the compressible Euler equations have been justified for smooth flows, with shock waves (Yu, 2005; Huang–Wang–Wang–Yang), with contact discontinuities, with rarefaction waves, and for stationary boundary-layer (Milne) problems (Esposito–Guo–Kim–Marra). However, a complete unified theory combining matched asymptotic expansions and convergence in the presence of both shocks and physical boundaries for the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic limits with shock waves of the Boltzmann equation
status_evidence.snippet: Piecewise smooth solutions with shocks of the Euler equations are obtained as the zero Knudsen number limit of Boltzmann equation solutions for hard sphere collisions.
status_evidence.claim: Shock-wave hydrodynamic limit justified for hard-sphere Boltzmann.

status_evidence.title: Stationary solutions to the Boltzmann equation in the hydrodynamic limit
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous estimates for the distance between kinetic and fluid-dynamic solutions in terms of the mean-free path are obtained when the interior fluid flow is smooth.
status_evidence.claim: Stationary boundary-layer hydrodynamic limit established for smooth interior flow.

status_evidence.title: The fluid-dynamic limit of the Broadwell model in the presence of shocks
status_evidence.snippet: Validity of the fluid dynamical approximation with shock layers for the Broadwell model.
status_evidence.claim: Shock-layer theory complete for Broadwell model but not general Boltzmann.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic Limit of the Boltzmann Equation to the Planar Rarefaction Wave
status_evidence.snippet: Limit to rarefaction waves justified in 3D.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on hydrodynamic limits with wave patterns.
